name: Project Handover Checklist
description: A clear plan to transfer a project to a new owner or team without losing knowledge.

items.text: Confirm the incoming owner and the handover date
Agree on an overlap period for questions and support
items.note: Even a week of overlap reduces costly gaps.

items.text: Tell stakeholders who their new point of contact will be
List everything that needs to transfer
Schedule the knowledge-transfer sessions in advance
Write a current status summary with open items
List active tasks, deadlines, and dependencies
Document known risks, issues, and workarounds
Record key decisions and the reasons behind them
Create a directory of key contacts and vendors
Note where all files and systems are located
List all systems, tools, and accounts in use
Grant the new owner the access they need
Transfer or reset shared passwords securely
items.note: Use a password manager, never plain email.

items.text: Reassign ownership of files, repos, and folders
Update licenses and subscriptions to the new owner
Confirm the incoming owner can log in to everything
Walk the new owner through the project end to end
Demonstrate recurring tasks and routine processes
Explain stakeholder relationships and expectations
Cover common problems and how to handle them
Record sessions or notes the owner can revisit
items.note: Recordings help when questions surface later.

items.text: Have the new owner complete a key task on their own
Review the handover document together for gaps
Confirm all access works as expected
Answer any remaining questions before stepping back
Agree on who to contact for follow-up issues
Confirm both owners agree the handover is complete
Get written sign-off from the manager or sponsor
Revoke the outgoing owner's access where appropriate
items.note: Remove old access promptly to keep systems secure.

items.text: Send a final note announcing the new owner
Archive the handover documents for reference

faq.a: It is the transfer of a project, system, or role from one owner to another. It moves documentation, access, and knowledge so the new owner can continue the work smoothly.

faq.q: What should a handover document include?
faq.a: Project status, key contacts, open tasks and risks, system access, recurring duties, and where files live. The goal is a single reference the new owner can rely on from day one.

faq.q: How do I do a good knowledge transfer?
faq.a: Combine clear documentation with live sessions. Walk the new owner through the work, answer questions, and overlap for a period so they can ask while you are still available.

faq.q: Who should be involved in a handover?
faq.a: The outgoing owner, the incoming owner, and the manager or sponsor who confirms the transfer. Key stakeholders should also be told who their new contact is.

faq.q: Can I print this project handover checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, work through it with both owners, and check off each item as documentation, access, and knowledge transfer are completed.
